markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least one of their own logged fair-share trials where the share came out to more than half a bar, and one where it came out to less than half a bar (actual bars and friends numbers from their own Investigation Record).
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine trials from the student's own record, correctly sorted into 'more than half' and 'less than half'.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim about shares with no actual bars/friends numbers quoted from their own trials.

markingScheme.criterion: States the general rule correctly: a share works out to more than half a bar exactly when the number of bars is more than half the number of friends.
markingScheme.accept: Equivalent wording, e.g. 'when there are more bars than half the number of friends'.

markingScheme.criterion: Links this back to fraction-as-division: explains that the size of each person's share is exactly what you get when you divide the number of bars by the number of friends.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating the numeric rule correctly with no mention of dividing bars by friends.

markingScheme.criterion: Scales the ratio 2:1 correctly for 6 people, giving 6 cups of flour and 3 cups of milk (multiplying both parts by the same scale factor, ×3).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct working showing the same scale factor applied to both ingredients.
markingScheme.insufficient: Changing only one ingredient amount, or scaling the two ingredients by different factors.

markingScheme.criterion: Recognises sharing 5 pancakes between 3 people as 5 ÷ 3, and expresses the answer as a fraction or mixed number (5/3 or 1 2/3).
markingScheme.accept: Any mathematically correct equivalent form (e.g. 1.67, accepted as an approximation of 1 2/3).
markingScheme.insufficient: Leaving the answer as '5 and 3' with no division performed, or giving only a whole-number answer.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains the different job each tool does: ratio keeps ingredients in the same proportion for a bigger batch, while division/fraction shares a finished total out equally between people.
markingScheme.insufficient: Describing only ratio OR only division, without contrasting what each one is for.

levels.descriptor: Achieves 0 of the 3 points above: no genuine trial figures are quoted, no general rule about bars vs. friends is stated, and no link is made to fraction-as-division.

Achieves 1 of the 3 points above — most commonly quotes at least one real trial (bars and friends numbers) but does not state the general rule correctly and/or does not link the result to dividing bars by friends.
Achieves 2 of the 3 points above — e.g. quotes genuine trial figures and states the general rule correctly, but does not also link this back to fraction-as-division (or vice versa).

Achieves all 3 of the points above: quotes genuine 'more than half' and 'less than half' trials from their own record, states the general rule correctly, and links the result to dividing the number of bars by the number of friends.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: Achieves 0 of the 3 points above: the ratio is not scaled correctly, the pancake share is not expressed as a division/fraction, and no distinction is drawn between ratio and division.

Achieves 1 of the 3 points above — most commonly scales the ratio correctly (6 cups flour, 3 cups milk) but does not correctly express 5 ÷ 3 as a fraction/mixed number, and/or does not explain why ratio and division are different tools.
Achieves 2 of the 3 points above — e.g. correctly scales the ratio and expresses 5 ÷ 3 as a fraction, but does not also explain the different job each tool does.

Achieves all 3 of the points above: scales the ratio correctly by the same factor for both ingredients, expresses 5 pancakes shared between 3 people as a correct fraction/mixed number, and explains why ratio (fixed proportion) and division (fair sharing) are different tools.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across both the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks above.

Understandable but with unclear phrasing or missing key terms such as ratio, numerator or denominator.
Clear, well-formed sentences using correct maths vocabulary.

markingInstructions: This is a Primary 2 student. Mark ONLY the two constructed responses, using each question's point-by-point marking_scheme in marking_context (award each point independently unless it names a dependsOn point, in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded) and each point's accept/insufficient wording. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity, never overlapping with the content marks. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Accept valid alternative wording or equivalent fractions/decimals; do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 14 (6 auto + 3 + 3 + 2). Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
